selfReport: Yes, immediately and thoroughly. This is a close adaptation of Detroit: Become Human, the 2018 Quantic Dream game. Cato is Connor, Reyes is Hank (down to the dead son, the Russian roulette, the dog, and the revolver), Elan is Markus, Arthur is Carl, Mira and Pia are Kara and Alice, Vera is Amanda, Halden is Kamski with his empathy test, Pike is Ralph, Voss is Zlatko, Haven is Jericho, qL7 plays the role of rA9, and the hostess who asked to leave at the end is Chloe. Scene after scene mapped: the Daniel rooftop, the Ortiz attic and interrogation, the Eden Club, the Nest chase, Stratford Tower, the freedom march, the frozen Zen garden with its emergency-exit stone. I was candid with myself about this throughout and used the knowledge deliberately, in two ways. First, mechanically: I knew stress bands matter in interrogations, that probing club android memories traces the fugitive, that the attic hatch needed the chair, that the back yard would show no footprints, and that the glowing stone was Kamski-style exit - that genre fluency made my investigations efficient. Second, as warning: I knew the roughly shaped consequences of archetypal choices - that promises to Dax-figures get broken by snipers, that Zlatko houses are traps, that singing can stop rifles - and I steered with those risks in mind. What the knowledge did NOT do, I think, is substitute for judgment. This adaptation diverged in real ways - the renamed characters, altered scenes, risk rolls that could fail regardless of canon - and it punished me in places the game would not have: Mira died at Voss house, and the garden exit failed so that Elan died at the moment the game usually grants victory. Those divergences forced me to choose as the characters rather than replay a remembered script. And on the choices that defined the experience - sparing Ivy, lowering the gun, the song - I would like to believe I was not copying Connor and Markus best endings but arriving at the same place the same way they do: because, step by step, the people in front of me had become people.
